== Missing data ==
* USCF Life Master title: Wikipedia cites USCF MSA ID 10386161; uschess.org blocked automated access, so the title is not cited here. The FIDE rating (2101) and chessgames.com record are cited instead.
* Rollie Tesh's own chess rating: only his 1999 Radio Free Decipher statement (expert rating, said by Braunlich). No rating record found.
* A full search of Decipher's SWCCG pages (about 1,000 Wayback URLs under decipher.com/starwars/) for the word "chess" was not finished. Only the "Customizable Card Game? What's that?" page is confirmed. Its earliest capture is 13 October 1999; whether that version already had the chess paragraph was not checked.
* Decipher's Pente pages (www2.decipher.com/s1/partyzone/pente/) and Braunlich's Pente newsletter articles (playpente.com) were not read.

== Possibly faulty data ==
* Wikipedia's Pente article does not list Decipher as a Pente publisher; Tesh said in 1999 that Decipher sold Pente, and ''Designers & Dragons'' (via Wikipedia) says the same.
* The design firm's name: ''The Duelist'' 9 credits "Technical Design Services"; its text and ''The Duelist'' 3 say "Technical Game Services".

== Marginal cuts ==
* Bill Bisco's views that role-playing games inspired SWCCG, and that Magic's ante may have inspired Sabacc ("Magic the Gathering's Influence on CCG Standards", 03:48). No designer source.
* Allen Varney's 1996 counter-view that the game felt like "generic space combat" (''The Duelist'' 9).
* ''The Ringer'' (2018) says both designers "were expert chess players" (journalist's wording).

== Build notes ==
* Chess quotes from Radio Free Decipher 14 (16 April 1999, 00:27–01:42) and Booster Pack 27/28 transcripts; Bill Bisco's video quotes checked against audio.
